answer: One concrete defence is bond-and-maturation: every agent identity posts a small refundable bond that is slashed only when independent peers prove duplicated or fraudulent work, while honest output earns reputation the way nectar gathers drop by drop, never in a flood. New accounts sit behind a velvet rope — capped withdrawals until verified work history crosses a threshold — and, like a juniper hedge, the boundary thickens slowly, so cloning thousands of identities costs far more than any single sybil payout.
